name: canRaise-restates-the-law-instead-of-asking-it
why: The restatement agrees with statUp everywhere except its clamp, which is exactly where a player would be offered a press the law refuses.

name: a-press-does-not-aim-before-it-presses
why: ORL1's incident one layer up: a press that acts on whatever the cursor was left on raises the wrong attribute, silently, on every click.

name: the-HIGHEST-major-is-dropped-from-the-sum
old: for (const id of majors) if (value(id) < value(lowest)) lowest = id;
new: for (const id of majors) if (value(id) > value(lowest)) lowest = id;
why: The ribbon would teach a player the opposite of PlayerEntity.SetCurrentLevelUpSkillSum.

name: the-WORST-minor-is-the-one-that-counts
old: for (const id of minors) if (value(id) > value(best)) best = id;
new: for (const id of minors) if (value(id) < value(best)) best = id;

name: the-oghma-is-promised-a-level-it-does-not-grant
why: applyLevelUp's oghma arm takes no Level++ (AUDIT 39), so this is the window lying about the one thing it is for.

name: the-commit-is-allowed-with-points-unspent
why: DFU's CheckIfDoneLeveling and the mod's validateLevelUp are the same sentence: all of it, or nothing.

name: two-stars-are-drawn-on-the-same-point
why: The figure is stretched to the stage, so a pair this close is two overlapping buttons on a phone - a point spent on the wrong attribute.

name: a-fortified-attribute-overflows-its-star
old: export const starBrightness = (value) => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (value ?? 0) / MAX_STAT_VALUE));

name: the-enhanced-skin-loses-its-level-up-window
old: if (isEnhanced() && typeof document !== 'undefined') return enhancedLevelUpOverlay(rollout(), deps.entity);

name: the-font-less-escape-cannot-recognise-the-DOM-window
why: scenes/dungeonContext.js asks by this name; a window it cannot recognise is nulled rather than closed, and stays on the screen over a game already handed back.
